name: Fimmvörðuháls pass
region: Between Eyjafjallajökull and Mýrdalsjökull, south Iceland
why: Up the Skógá past twenty-six waterfalls, across the still-warm lava of the 2010 eruption between two ice caps, and down a narrow ridge into the green of Þórsmörk.
book: Free. Take the highland bus back from Básar (Þórsmörk), booked ahead; the Baldvinsskáli hut on the pass can be booked through Ferðafélag Íslands to split the walk in two.
water: Fill up from the Skógá before the footbridge: from there to Þórsmörk there is only snowmelt, the hut on the pass has no running water.
dangers: The pass is above 1,000 m: fog, snow and gale-force wind even in July. Turn back to Skógar if it closes in.
Snowfields of about 200 m on the pass all summer: follow the poles.
Heljarkambur and Kattahryggir are narrow ridges with drops on both sides; a chain helps on Heljarkambur.
turnaround: Be at the footbridge over the Skógá by 12:00; if you see no poles ahead on the pass, go back down.

points.name: Skógafoss, Skógar
points.note: The stairs on the right of the 60 m fall lead to the top, where the path follows the river north.

points.name: The Skógá waterfalls
points.note: Twenty-six falls in the first 8 km above Skógafoss, each different; the path keeps to the east rim.

points.name: Baldvinsskáli hut
points.note: The A-frame hut where the pass begins, about 920 m, after the footbridge and the long gravel climb; no running water.

points.name: Magni and Móði craters
points.note: The two red cinder cones of the 2010 eruption on the pass; the black Goðahraun lava is still warm under the surface in places.

points.name: Heljarkambur ridge
points.note: The narrow ridge down to Morinsheiði, with a chain on the worst step. Þórsmörk opens below.

points.name: Básar hut, Þórsmörk
points.note: The Útivist hut in the birch woods of Goðaland, where the highland buses stop.
